title: Release gate: run the qualified binary against a feature of THIS release, with the prior release as the negative control (DEC-204 (b), QCLI-438 precedent)
description:
DEC-204 (OPAG-1419) rules that lore ships prebuilt platform binaries, so the fix rule already applied to quest-cli in QCLI-438 applies here too. This task files the gate half (b) only: no build-identity work.

WHAT WAS MEASURED on origin/dev 35d5ce13. The package-qualification job in .github/workflows/release.yml builds each platform binary from the checkout, and the report records repository.commit by running git rev-parse HEAD in the build job (benchmark/ladybug/package-qualification.ts:505, recorded at :461). The workflow asserts that value equals github.sha (release.yml:617-629, re-asserted at :748-758). It also records platformTarballSha256 (:474) and compares it with a digest recomputed from the same artifact (:748-759); standaloneBinarySha256 (:475) has no consumer anywhere. The binary prints only its version (src/cli.ts:251, src/meta.ts:7) and no commit is embedded in it (benchmark/ladybug/package-build.ts:36-45).

So the gate currently proves the CHECKOUT was at the dispatch commit, and that one artifact survived transport between jobs. It never runs the produced binary to prove it carries this release behavior.

SCOPE. In the release run, the gate must execute the qualified host-platform binary against a feature that exists only in THIS release source tree, and exit nonzero when the binary lacks it. In the same run, the PREVIOUS release published binary runs the same command as the negative control and must fail. Prove both ways: a deliberately stale binary goes red, and a fresh build of the release tree goes green.

The feature is the implementer choice, but it must be a behavior this release actually adds rather than a version string, and its absence must be observable. One shape: a command or flag added by the release, asserted present on the new binary and absent on the previous one.

DEPENDENCY AND PROCESS. This task blocks the pair-release prep (LCLI-714, opum-ai/lore-cli#572), which stays held behind it. It touches CI workflows, so it is on the DEC-182 floor: built on DeepSeek with a Stage 1 review, and opum-doc does an Opus review by ref before landing.

OUT OF SCOPE, deliberately not build work here: the stronger build-identity binding (an embedded commit verified from the binary, or a tarball attestation) and LCLI-482. opum-doc is taking that as a design question.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The release gate runs the qualified host-platform binary against a feature introduced by this release source tree, and the run exits nonzero when the binary lacks that feature.
In the same run, the previous release published binary runs the same command as a negative control, and the gate requires that command to fail.
The gate is proven both ways: a deliberately stale binary produces a red result and a fresh build of the release tree produces a green result, with the evidence for both recorded on this task.
The gate is wired into .github/workflows/release.yml so that no publish can proceed without it.
